title: How to sell an Amazon FBA business: valuation, buyers, and what raises the price
summary: A buyer-first guide to selling an Amazon FBA business. It covers which business types sell (proprietary > private label > reseller), how to value it with SDE and EBITDA, the factors that raise the multiple, who buys at each price tier, and typical sale timelines.

principles.text: Sell from the buyer's perspective; ignoring it leaves your listing sitting for months.
principles.quote: You must always consider the perspective of the buyer. Without putting yourself in their shoes, your Amazon business for sale could sit on the listings for months.

principles.text: Proprietary and private-label products sell far better than reseller businesses, which buyers see as risky.
principles.quote: In this case, only your company sells the product, and therefore, buyers will pay a premium to get it.

principles.text: Keep immaculate, current books; clean P&L records remove a reason for buyers to walk away.
principles.quote: Buyers are often looking for that one reason not to buy your Amazon business. Therefore, having your books in order eliminates at least one reason for the buyer to turn away.

principles.text: Rule-of-thumb valuation: roughly 2x annual net profit (SDE), with inventory bought at cost on top.
principles.quote: The rule of thumb is to take your annual net profit and multiply it by two.

principles.text: Diversify to cut risk: multiple products and niches, traffic outside Amazon, and no single product above 70% of income.
principles.quote: Avoid having one product or niche bringing in more than 70% of your Amazon business' income.

principles.text: Defensibility raises value: proprietary products, brand loyalty, and higher quality than copycats make market share hard to steal.
principles.quote: If you have a patent for your product, your business's value will increase.
